sanskrit_verse:
परस्त्रीपानसक्ताश्च कितवाः पूर्वदूषिताः ।
उन्मत्तार्ताः साहसिकाः नास्तिकाश्च न साक्षिणः ॥
transliteration: parastrīpānasaktāś ca kitavāḥ pūrvadūṣitāḥ | unmattārtāḥ sāhasikā nāstikāś ca na sākṣiṇaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Those attached to another's spouse, gamblers, previously defamed persons, the distressed insane, the violent, and the atheist — these are not witnesses.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority stems from alignment with Sanatana Dharma, not personal desire or distortion.
Causation is traced through consciousness disruption and misalignment with Satya.
Capacity-based responsibility requires mental and spiritual integrity as prerequisites.
Restoration logic demands removal of compromised elements from truth-establishing processes.
Consciousness alignment determines eligibility to uphold or testify in matters of Dharma.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person exhibits parastrīpāna-sakti (attachment to another’s spouse), THEN disqualify from witness capacity.
IF a person is identified as kitava (gambler), THEN exclude from judicial testimony roles.
IF a person has been previously dūṣita (defamed due to moral misconduct), THEN invalidate as legal witness.
IF a person is unmatta (insane) or ārta (distressed), THEN defer testimony until consciousness stabilization.
IF a person displays sāhasa (violence) or nāstika-bhāva (denial of Dharma), THEN disallow participation in truth-bearing procedures.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, any individual bearing traits listed in this śloka must be excluded from witness eligibility. The threshold of responsibility includes not just action but ontological alignment with Sanatana Dharma. Witness validity is determined by consciousness stability and dharmic integrity, not mere legal standing.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality identifies that distorted consciousness leads to unreliable perception. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that moral and spiritual degradation precedes factual distortion. Responsibility is proportional to one’s alignment with Satya. This exclusion serves restoration, not punishment — ensuring only those aligned with Dharma participate in truth establishment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Śuddhi processes for disqualified individuals to restore consciousness integrity.
Assign Vedic study and discipline under qualified gurus for reintegration into societal functions.
Establish Dharmic rehabilitation centers focusing on character reconstruction before re-engagement.
Implement completion rituals for past distortions to ensure karmic resolution without punitive overlay.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Dharma. Exclusion from witness-hood is not punitive but restorative. Reality operates beyond retribution. Consciousness remains the sole adjudicator. Dharma is restored.
